content.thinking:
I'm checking the first overview claim against the record: every account page render calls the card lookup, and the root cause ticket supports that account pages in io-shop were failing on it, so the "some shoppers" wording holds. Next I'm verifying the duration claim, which the figures appear to back up.

I'm going through the remaining overview claims one by one: the peak error rate and the estimated customer loss are figures I'll check against the record, and the on-call and resolution points match what the record says. I'm also confirming why no code fix was pursued, since the fault sits in another company's service.

I'm checking the fourth overview claim against the record and I'm not sure the "no code fix" reasoning holds. The record gives the reason as the failure sitting in another company's service, but the contributing factors also say io-shop had no fallback, and the second action item is a code change in io-shop. So "the fault is not in the shop's own code" isn't quite the record's reason, and I'll flag it.

flags.quote: it did not look for a code fix because the fault is not in the shop's own code
flags.why: The record gives the reason as the failure being in a service another company runs that nothing Argus can do reaches, and it names io-shop's own lack of a fallback as a contributing factor (AI-2), so it does not say the shop's code played no part.

supported.quote: The cause was IO Payments Ltd, the outside payment company that the shop asks for a shopper's saved card. It started rejecting those requests, and every time a request failed, the account page failed too.
At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing.
